summary: P1b WS-5 Alembic main consumer check/config: verify and, if needed, wire Alembic main's PathGuard/runtime configuration for host context managed guidance writes after accepted Core + Plugin WS-5 work.
sourceRef: Design/docs/current/alembic-proactive-activation-2026-07-03.md §10.0 §10.5 §10.6; accepted Core tc-20260707080952-0013 / commit 783b9f52aaa83767f4564ac8489cdfaf445bab35; accepted Plugin tc-20260707082929-0017 / commit 33f2954901723abf85214abcae0cebaabb4cb1d4.
designIntent: The requirement scope explicitly includes Alembic main for WS-5 pathGuard configure expansion. This package keeps that boundary narrow: prove whether main has a real WS-5 consumer path, and implement only the minimal PathGuard/managed-block configuration if the main source owns such a consumer.

targetTasks.summary: Read AGENTS.md, the state root, Alembic/AGENTS.md, Design/docs/current/alembic-proactive-activation-2026-07-03.md §10.0/§10.5/§10.6, and the accepted Core + Plugin controller review evidence before editing. Implement only the Alembic main side of WS-5 if a real main consumer exists: inspect AppRuntime/Bootstrap PathGuard configuration and the in-process project-skill/cold-start delivery path, then add the minimal pathGuard.addProjectWritableFile-style configuration or Core managed-block consumption needed so main-owned code can safely write/remove only the selected host context file (codex => AGENTS.md, claude-code => CLAUDE.md) without weakening unrelated root-file protection. Do not duplicate Plugin ProjectSkillService, do not edit AlembicPlugin or AlembicCore, do not implement WS-2 host-aware skill export, WS-3 onboarding, or WS-6 cold-start auto-sync. If Alembic main has no WS-5 host-guidance write surface after the accepted Plugin implementation, return completed with no-commit evidence naming the searched entrypoints and why no code change is needed. Acceptance evidence: commit hash or explicit no-commit reason; file/line review of PathGuard configuration and any main-owned skill-delivery/cold-start consumer; tests/build/check proving no root-file guard weakening; risks and exact next-phase recommendation.
